title: IRMV humanoid ONNX policy deployment contract, version 1
$comment: The value of the single model-level metadata key `irmv.deployment` of a policy ONNX, encoded as UTF-8 JSON. The SDK parses it with irmv::policy::ParseDeployment into the DeploymentContract of include/irmv/policy/deployment.hpp and refuses every model whose key is absent, duplicated, of another schema_version or of another policy_type; it never falls back to a hard-coded array of an older SDK. Conforming validation MUST evaluate the irmv-joint-name format as a nonempty string whose UTF-8 encoding is at most 64 bytes; validators that ignore format annotations do not implement this contract. JSON Schema cannot express the finiteness rule, so it is stated here: ParseDeployment rejects every NaN and Infinity anywhere in the document, and it rejects any null that is not one of the explicitly nullable fields of `clip` and `source` (a null of `source` must additionally be listed in `source.missing`, so an absent provenance fact is always explained). The document is descriptive: it never changes the computation graph, its inputs or its outputs, and it never executes PD, scaling or clipping - the SDK implements those from this contract. All gains and targets are joint-output-side quantities in rad, rad/s, N*m, N*m/rad and N*m*s/rad.

policy_type.$comment: The only policy type this phase implements: the model output is a normalized joint position action that the contract below scales, offsets and clips into a q target.

input.$comment: The observation tensor the SDK feeds. Its dimension must equal the sum over `observation.terms` of the term dimensions, and the name must equal the input name of the loaded ONNX.

output.$comment: The action tensor the SDK reads. Its dimension must equal the number of `action.joints`, and the name must equal the output name of the loaded ONNX.

policy_period_us.$comment: The period one policy step is expected to take, derived on the training side from sim.dt * decimation (0.005 s * 4 = 20 ms = 50 Hz for the recorded training run). The application uses it as the inference cadence and as the fresh-result deadline; it is not a runtime safety parameter.

joints.$comment: The deployment joint names of the action vector, in the order the model output uses. ParseDeployment resolves them by exact name against robot.joints[].name and refuses a model joint the deployment does not have.

source_joints.$comment: The joint names the training asset actually resolved for this list, element-wise aligned with `joints`. They are the explicit, checkable mapping between the training asset (for example `left_hip_pitch_joint`) and the deployment name (for example `left_hip_pitch`): the exporter must derive them from the instantiated asset, never from a guess, and the field keeps the mapping in the model package instead of in a separate file.

default_q.$comment: rad; the default joint positions of the action joints, one per entry of `joints`, as the instantiated asset resolved them (asset default joint positions, including the per-joint regex rules of the training configuration).

default_dq.$comment: rad/s; the default joint velocities, one per entry of `joints`.

kp.$comment: N*m/rad, joint output side, one per entry of `joints`. The action term's stiffness as the training configuration resolved it (the recorded run: 100 for hip yaw/roll/pitch and knee, 60 for ankle pitch/roll).

kd.$comment: N*m*s/rad, one per entry of `joints` (the recorded run: 6 and 4).

scale.$comment: The action scale of the action term, one per entry of `joints` (0.5 for the recorded run).

offset.$comment: rad; the resolved action offset, one per entry of `joints`. With `use_default_offset=true` this is the resolved default joint position, not the raw `offset=0.0` of the configuration file.

wrapper.$comment: The clip the training runner applies to the raw policy output before the environment sees it (agent.clip_actions). null means no clipping, which is the recorded run.

term.$comment: The clip the action term applies after scale and offset (actions.joint_pos.clip). null means no clipping, which is the recorded run. agent.algorithm.clip_param is the PPO surrogate clip and is never this value.

order.$comment: The frozen pipeline order. Exactly ["wrapper_clip","scale","offset","term_clip"], matching isaaclab JointAction.process_actions (raw * scale + offset, then the term clip) preceded by the runner's raw-action clip; ParseDeployment refuses any other order instead of guessing one.

stage.$comment: Which action the `last_action` observation holds. The recorded run observes the raw action (isaaclab mdp.last_action returns action_manager.action, the action the policy emitted before scale, offset and the term clip); `processed` names the post-pipeline q target.

initial.$comment: The value the last_action history starts from when a behavior is entered, one per entry of `joints`; all zeros for the recorded run, which is what the training action manager resets to.

terms.$comment: The policy observation group in concatenation order. ParseDeployment requires exactly the six supported terms in exactly this order: command, projected_gravity, base_ang_vel, joint_pos_rel, joint_vel_rel, last_action. Each position pins the name, the unit and the frame of its term, so a document cannot claim a meaning this build does not implement. A YAML dictionary or an uninstantiated configuration must never be the source of this order.

joint_pos_rel.$comment: rad; `reference` is the resolved default joint position the term subtracts, element-wise aligned with `joints`. It is the same value as action.default_q only when the action and the observation resolve the same joint list, which is checked rather than assumed.

joint_vel_rel.$comment: rad/s; `reference` is the resolved default joint velocity the term subtracts.

enabled.$comment: Whether the trained policy normalizes its actor observation at all (agent.policy.actor_obs_normalization). false for the recorded run: no normalizer is applied and no statistics are needed.

embedded.$comment: Whether the normalization is already part of the ONNX graph instead of being an application-side step. Must be false when `enabled` is false. true means the SDK must not normalize again.

location.$comment: Where the normalization happens: `none` when disabled, `model` when the graph embeds it, `application` when the SDK must apply it from `algorithm`/`statistics`.

algorithm.$comment: Required when `enabled` is true. The only supported semantics: (x - mean) / std per observation component, component-wise, applied to the concatenated observation before inference. Any other algorithm is refused.

count.$comment: The number of samples the statistics were accumulated from.

std.$comment: Per component, element-wise aligned with the concatenated observation; strictly positive and finite.

statistics.$comment: Required when the normalizer is enabled and not embedded; forbidden otherwise. An enabled model without its statistics is refused, because the SDK would otherwise have to guess the normalization.

checkpoint_file.$comment: Path or file name of the checkpoint the model was exported from.

env_config_file.$comment: Path or file name of the serialized training environment configuration (params/env.yaml).

agent_config_file.$comment: Path or file name of the serialized training agent configuration (params/agent.yaml).

asset_revision.$comment: Revision or digest of the robot asset the environment instantiated.

software.$comment: Software versions the export depended on, for example isaaclab, rsl_rl, torch, python, onnx. May be empty when nothing could be read.

missing.$comment: The names of the fields above that could not be determined, spelled exactly as the property name (for example "checkpoint_sha256"). Every null field must appear here, and no other name may: an unexplained null is refused, so a package never claims provenance it does not have.

jointName.$comment: maxLength counts code points; the contract is 1..64 UTF-8 bytes.

jointNameList.$comment: Duplicate names inside one list are refused.

finiteNumber.$comment: Finite: NaN and Infinity are refused wherever a number appears.

gainArray.$comment: Finite and non-negative. A pure feed-forward command (kp = kd = 0, tau_ff != 0) is legal; the runtime performs the final torque limiting.

scalarLayer.$comment: The shape of an observation term scale: absent, or one finite factor per component of the term.

scale.$comment: null or one factor per component of the term; the training configuration leaves every scale null.

clip.$comment: null or one range per component of the term; applied to the term value after its scale.

history_length.$comment: 0 or 1 mean the term is not stacked; a term with a longer history is refused, because this phase ships no history stacking.

unit.$comment: Body-frame forward velocity, lateral velocity and yaw rate, in this order.

dimension.$comment: Must equal the length of observation.joint_pos_rel.joints, which JSON Schema cannot express; ParseDeployment checks it.
Must equal the length of observation.joint_vel_rel.joints; ParseDeployment checks it.
Must equal the length of action.joints; ParseDeployment checks it.

term.$comment: The observation term this list belongs to.

joints.$comment: Deployment joint names, in the order the term concatenates them; must equal the joint list the term's dimension implies.

reference.$comment: The reference the term subtracts, one per entry of `joints`: the resolved default joint position in rad for joint_pos_rel, the resolved default joint velocity in rad/s for joint_vel_rel.
